Treaty between the United States of America and the Republic of Panama Concerning the Treatment and Protection of Investments (signed 1982; in force 1991)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 25 of 12 June 1995 on Private Interest Foundations, as amended; Law 23 of 27 April 2015 on AML/CFT, implemented by Executive Decree 363 of 2015, as amended; Law 70 of 2019 on Beneficial Ownership and Customer Due Diligence; Law 129 of 2020 establishing the National Final Beneficiary Register administered by the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI/MEF) under Resolución DGI 2021-1887 and related amendments; binding resolutions of the Superintendencia de Sujetos No Financieros (SSNF) and OFAC-aligned OFAC/GAFILAT-derived supervisory standards applicable to licensed resident agents.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the Founder's passport (bio-page and acknowledgment page), notarized
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent notary of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Panama is a State Party to the Hague Apostille Convention of 5 October 1961)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and confirmation of source of funds/worth concerning the Founder(s)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization for issuers in non-Hague countries

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing, Articles of Association, and direct/indirect shareholder chart of the corporate Founder (if applicable)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry of the Founder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO declaration and source-of-wealth statement (SSNF/DGI-compliant PIF KYC pack) signed by the Founder and each Council member
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panamanian resident agent (licensed law firm) and/or Notary Public

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Spanish translation of all non-Spanish due-diligence and charter documents

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations Law), as amended by Ley No. 32 de 2 de junio de 2011, Articles 1, 4, 5, 6, 7, 13, 20 and 22; complemented by Ley No. 21 de 2017 (beneficial ownership transparency), the Public Registry of Panama regulations, and the Municipal Aviso de Operación regime under Ley 66 de 1947.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry of Panama) - Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acta de Fundación (Foundation Charter) and Reglamento (Foundation Regulations) formalized before a Notario Público and inscribed in the Public Registry of Panama
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Article 13 of Law 25 of 1995 requires an initial endowment of not less than US$10,000 (equivalent of B/.10,000). No escrow or blocked bank account is mandatory: the endowment obligation may be satisfied by the Founder's written declaration of contribution of cash, assets, receivables, or inventory, which the first Foundation Council must accept and record in the incorporation minutes.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION No. 001/2025 OF THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL OF [FOUNDATION NAME] FOUNDATION. The members of the Foundation Council, duly convened by the Founder, hereby resolve unanimously: 1. To accept the Founder's declaration of initial endowment of US$10,000 in accordance with Article 13 of Law 25 of 1995. 2. To adopt the Foundation Regulations presented with the Foundation Charter. 3. To fix the registered office in Panama City, Panama, and ratify the appointment of the Resident Agent, the Protector, and the Council officers named in the Charter. 4. To open the statutory records and instruct the Chairman to request inscription with the Public Registry of Panama. 5. To certify that this resolution has been passed and authorize its attestation before a Notary Public for registration purposes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name availability search and certificate of no objection
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Departamento de Certificados, via the online certificate platform of the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a name clearance request for the proposed Private Interest Foundation name, which must include the word 'Fundación' and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered entity. The Registry issues the Certificado de No Objeción, reserving the name for 30 days. Verify the certificate for correct spelling and scope before proceeding.
required_dossiers: Signed name search application form
Notarized copy of the power of attorney of the applicant law firm (if applicable)
Passport or identity card of the applicant or Founder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or flagged as confusingly similar, submit a new application with up to three alternative names and pay the reduced re-search fee. An administrative reconsideration may be lodged with the Director of the Public Registry within 5 business days of the refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, execution and notarization of the Foundation Charter and Regulations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notario Público (Notary Public) of the Republic of Panama, Panama City
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Founder, or its attorney-in-fact, executes the Acta de Fundación and the Reglamento before a Panamanian Notary Public. The notary verifies identity, capacity, and the Spanish text of the instruments; the Charter must state the Founder's name and domicile, the Foundation's name, purpose, initial endowment, instructions, Council members, Protector, registered agent, and duration. If the endowment includes real property located in Panama, the instrument must be raised to a public deed. The notary retains the protocol and issues authorized first copies.
required_dossiers: Draft Acta de Fundación (Foundation Charter) in Spanish
Draft Reglamento (Foundation Regulations) in Spanish
Original power of attorney if the Founder acts through a representative
Passport or identity card of the Founder and each Foundation Council member
Written declaration of initial endowment of at least US$10,000
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or the Registry's draft-review identifies a defective clause, amend the document by marginal notation and re-execute the signatures, paying only the additional notarial page fee; no new application is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apostille and legalization of foreign documents (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Legalizaciones y Apostillas, Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Where the Founder, officers, or corporate shareholders act through foreign instruments, such documents must be translated into Spanish by an authorized translator and apostilled under the Hague Apostille Convention before presentation to the Public Registry. Submit the original foreign instruments to the Legalizations Department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, which will certify the signature of the foreign notary or issuing authority by affixing the apostille.
required_dossiers: Original foreign power of attorney or corporate resolutions
Certified Spanish translation of each foreign instrument
Apostille application form of the Legalizations Department
Proof of payment of the apostille fee (approximately US$20 per document)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the apostille is rejected for missing certification of the foreign authority's signature, return the instrument to the originating notary or competent authority abroad, obtain the proper notarial seal, and re-submit with a supplementary translation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Public Registry of Panama (Private Interest Foundations Section)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the notarized Acta de Fundación and Reglamento, together with the appointment of the Foundation Council, Protector, and registered agent, to the Foundations Section of the Public Registry. The Registry verifies legal formalities, assigns the Foundation's registration number in the Book of Foundations, and inscribes the Foundation. Upon approval, the Registry issues the inscription certificate and stamped copies.
required_dossiers: Notarized first copy of the Acta de Fundación
Notarized Reglamento
Certificate of No Objection (name clearance)
Written acceptance of office signed by the registered agent
Qualified professional license and address of the registered agent (lawyer or law firm)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a defect or observación, the registered agent must correct the noted articles, re-notarize the amendment, and re-file; the Registry resolves the query within 10 business days upon full compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining the tax identification number (RUC and NIT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas de Panamá, through the Sede Electrónica DGI portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After inscription, apply for the Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) and the Número de Identificación Tributaria (NIT) for the Foundation through the DGI's online taxpayer portal. Provide the inscription certificate, the registered agent's details, and the Foundation's purpose. Because the Foundation's fiscal status is territorial, the DGI will enroll it under the non-commercial or special regime unless it declares a Panamanian-source taxable activity; a sworn statement confirming no Panamanian-source income should be filed within 30 days of registration to preserve the tax-exempt status.
required_dossiers: Public Registry inscription certificate
Copy of the registered Foundation Charter and Regulations
Registered agent's RUC certificate
DGI Form 021 (taxpayer registration)
Registered office domicile and contact data
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI delays or queries the application, the registered agent may appear at the DGI taxpayer services window to correct the data or file an administrative reconsideration; the RUC is provisionally issued upon presentation of the inscription certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal operating notice (Aviso de Operación) for the physical warehouse activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alcaldía de Panamá - Dirección de Aviso de Operación / Ventanilla Única Municipal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Where the Foundation or its operating branch conducts kitting, fulfillment, and light assembly at a physical warehouse in Panama, file the Aviso de Operación with the Municipality, declaring the ISIC 5210 activity, the warehouse address, and estimated personnel. The Municipality issues the operating certificate and sets the annual municipal fee based on declared capital and workforce. The fire safety inspection must be coordinated with the Fire Department before the certificate is issued.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate of the operating entity
Lease agreement or ownership certificate of the warehouse premises
Zoning certificate (Certificado de Uso de Suelo)
Fire safety clearance from the Cuerpo de Bomberos
Identity documents of the legal representative
Completed Aviso de Operación form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Municipality rejects the notice for insufficient zoning or fire-safety documents, remedy by obtaining the Certificado de Uso de Suelo from the Municipal Urban Development Directorate and the Visto Bueno de Bomberos, then re-file within 30 days without penalty if operations have not yet commenced.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) - Dirección General de Empresas, for national industrial registration where applicable; Alcaldía de Panamá - Dirección de Aviso de Operación, as the primary issuer of the physical operating permit for ISIC 5210 warehousing and kitting activities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación (Municipal Operating Notice) for the warehouse/kitting facility; no separate national sectoral concession is required for ISIC 5210 light value-added postponement packaging, but the municipal permit, fire clearance, and environmental registration are mandatory conditions precedent to lawful operation.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente de Panamá (MiAMBIENTE) - Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I (Documentation / Informe Ambiental) under Law 41 de 1998 and Executive Decree 123 de 2009 for covered storage and kitting facilities exceeding 1,000 m² of construction or 5,000 m² of plot area; small packing-only premises below such thresholds are classified as not subject to the SEIA. A Full Environmental Impact Assessment (Category II or III) is triggered only if the facility handles hazardous waste, installs combustion boilers above 5 MW, or is located within protected buffer zones.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Sanitary wastewater must comply with Executive Decree 179 de 2006 (discharge to public sewer: pH 6-9, BOD5 not exceeding 300 mg/L, TSS not exceeding 350 mg/L, temperature below 40°C); no industrial process effluent is expected from kitting and assembly. VOC emissions from adhesives, shrink-wrap, or label printing must remain below the WHO community exposure values adopted by MiAMBIENTE (e.g., benzene not exceeding 0.005 mg/m³ annual average; toluene not exceeding 0.26 mg/m³ weekly average) and must be controlled by local exhaust ventilation or capture at source. Non-hazardous solid waste must be segregated, stored, and transported by MiAMBIENTE-licensed haulers under Resolution 659 de 2012, with scrap and empty containers inventoried and sent to authorized recyclers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Visto Bueno de Bomberos (Fire Safety Certificate) issued by the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá before opening, covering fire extinguishers, emergency exits, signage, and evacuation plans; structural load inspection of racks and mezzanines by the Municipal Engineering Directorate where storage height exceeds 1.8 m; registration of the workplace with the Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL) and enrollment of personnel in the Caja de Seguro Social (CSS); compliance with the industrial health and safety rules of Decree 40 de 1968, including first aid equipment, fire hydrants, ventilation, and a written health and safety plan.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Panama; digital portal: E-TAX 3.0 (Sistema Integrado de Tributación) — etax.mef.gob.pa, with SIME web services for filings and fiscal clearance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The Private Interest Foundation (PIF) must first be duly registered at the Registro Público under Law 25 of 1995. Before commencing commercial activity, the foundation, through its resident legal representative and a licensed public accountant, must apply to the DGI for a RUC (Registro Unico de Contribuyentes) via the E-TAX 3.0 portal or DGI window, attaching the certified foundation charter, public registration certificate, appointment record of the foundation council, and notarised identification of the resident agent. The DGI assigns the RUC and, where commercial activity is declared, concurrently registers the foundation for ITBMS and relevant withholding registrations; the foundation must separately register with the Caja de Seguro Social (CSS) if it has Panamanian employees.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists under Panamanian law. A PIF is a distinct juridical person taxed at entity level exclusively on Panama-source income under the territorial regime (Código Fiscal); foreign-source income of the foundation remains outside Panamanian tax. Available elections include: (i) irrevocable election to be treated as an ordinary commercial taxpayer when the foundation engages in habitual business; (ii) election into the small-taxpayer simplified ITBMS regime for gross income at or below PAB 36,000 per annum; (iii) elective registration in the official exporter registry to access 0% export supplies; and (iv) election into the SEM multinational headquarters regime under Law 41 of 2019. Hybrid mismatch and transparent entity elections are not available; Law 254 of 2021 controlled foreign corporation rules apply.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS — Impuesto a la Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (Panamanian VAT-type transfer tax on goods and services)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No minimum ITBMS registration threshold for exporters or persons performing taxable transfers in Panama, but an optional simplified small-taxpayer regime applies where annual gross income does not exceed PAB 36,000; registration becomes mandatory at PAB 36,000 or immediately upon commencement of taxable activities, whichever is earlier.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates real-time electronic invoicing for all ITBMS registrants through E-TAX 3.0 (phased implementation concluded for all taxpayers). Every invoice, including zero-rated export invoices, must be transmitted before issuance to the DGI fiscal control system via certified API/web service, must receive a unique acceptance folio and QR code, and must be archived digitally for the statutory six-year limitation period; export invoicing additionally requires the export invoice to be linked to the corresponding DUA customs declaration.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% ITBMS applies where (i) tangible goods are definitively exported and depart Panamanian customs territory under a valid DUA; or (ii) the services qualify as an export of services — rendered to a non-resident recipient, with legal and economic benefit occurring abroad, under Law 18 of 2019 and DGI Resolution ITBMS-2014. A PIF supplying fulfillment, kitting, and light assembly may zero-rate only the service element that is contractually and documentarily tied to goods that are exported to the foreign principal, evidenced by cross-border contracts, foreign purchase orders, title-transfer documents, and completed customs entries; logistics and warehousing consumed physically inside Panama for domestic goods remain subject to 7% ITBMS.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Declaración Unica Aduanera (DUA) — Customs Export Declaration, definitively accepted by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas
Bill of Lading (House or Master B/L, AWB, or truck manifest) evidencing physical exit of goods
Certificado de Ingreso de Divisas — inward foreign-currency remittance certificate issued by a Panamanian licensed bank and reported to SIMEX
Export commercial invoice issued in E-TAX 3.0 bearing the DGI fiscal QR and marked as export invoice
Supporting contract documentation: foreign purchase order, packing list, insurance certificate, and proof of transfer of risk and title
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI audit of export zero-rating claims may recharacterise unsupported exports as taxable domestic supplies, applying 7% ITBMS to the gross value on a retrospective basis, monthly surcharge interest of 1.5% (or fraction thereof), and fines of 10% up to 100% of the omitted tax under Código Fiscal Articles 758-762; fraudulent export zero-rating or false documentation constitutes tax evasion under Código Fiscal Article 775, punishable by 2 to 5 years of imprisonment, exclusion from the exporter registry, forfeiture of goods, and retroactive cancellation of export certificates with full tax clawback and criminal fines.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: No formal central bank exists for Panama. Monetary policy is effectively determined through official dollarization (US Federal Reserve), while the Banco Nacional de Panamá serves as fiscal agent and clearing conduit for government transactions. Prudential supervision of banks is vested in the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP), and the Dirección Nacional de Recaudación (DGI) enforces tax and FATCA/CRS reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility and unrestricted transfer of funds are guaranteed for both current and capital account transactions. Panama is a fully dollarized economy; the US Dollar is legal tender and the Balboa is a nominal unit at 1:1 parity. Profit remittance and capital repatriation are unlimited, but outbound dividends and branch remittances sourced from Panamanian-source income attract withholding tax under the territorial tax regime. Foreign currency accounts are permitted and no surrender or conversion requirements apply.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory requirement exists to surrender export proceeds to any monetary authority, nor is any compulsory conversion into local currency mandated. Exporters and service providers may hold export receipts in US Dollars or any freely convertible foreign currency in accounts at licensed Panamanian banks or foreign banks. However, cash transactions exceeding USD 10,000 must be reported under SBP AML/CFT rules, and disciplinary tax non-compliance may require furnishing of bank records to the DGI.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Corporate Account for warehousing and kitting operations
Treasury and Escrow Settlement Account for government-linked or contract-bound flows
Operational and Trade Settlement Account with LC and wire facilities
Capital Escrow Account and International Custody Account for foundation-held receivables
Dual-Currency Operational Account (USD and EUR) for cross-border supplier payables

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility is Low as a primary settlement rail and Moderate as an auxiliary receivables/payables channel. Panamanian law requires any payment service provider conducting deposit-taking or clearing activities for residents to be licensed by the SBP. Offshore digital EMI providers such as Airwallex, Revolut Business, or Payoneer can support invoicing and card payables, but they cannot replace a SBP-regulated local clearing account for ACH/Direct wire settlements. The Virtual Asset Service Provider Act (Law 62 of 2023, updated by Law 80 of 2024) further restricts unlicensed crypto/fintech overlay activities.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Most tier-1 Panamanian banks mandate physical attendance of at least one registered council member or the foundation's designated resident agent during initial onboarding. Remote videoconference opening is exceptionally permitted for low-risk structures with pre-existing banking relationships or where the final beneficiaries are OECD residents subject to ETIAS-level due diligence. The PIF must evidence its true commercial purpose and meet the SBP's enhanced due diligence standards; a simple virtual opening with no bank genesis is unlikely to succeed without a physical interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Private Interest Foundation (PIF) label cited as opaque offshore conduit
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized Foundation Charter and Regulations; authenticated Certificate of Incumbency from the resident agent showing lawful founders; legal opinion from a Panamanian counsel confirming no prohibited fiduciary features; comprehensive beneficial ownership declaration naming settlor, members of the council, and protector (if any); audited financial statements or a detailed opening balance sheet evidencing legitimate seed capital and kitting inventory; three years of projected cash flow and third-party logistics service contracts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership and remote original jurisdiction without substantial physical footprint
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copies of directors'/settlor's passports and proof of residence; utility bills not older than 90 days; professional references from a home-country regulated bank or law firm; evidence of an operational lease or licensed 3PL subcontract in Panama; detailed business plan for ISIC 5210 warehousing, kitting, and assembly services; exhibit of wholly third-party wholesale purchase orders and final consumer shipping profiles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cash-intensive or general-commerce clearing patterns typical of fulfillment businesses
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: AML transaction monitoring narrative describing customer onboarding controls, expected transaction frequency and size, and counterparty jurisdiction matrix; supply-chain contracts with named international shippers and freight forwarders; sample ASNs and shipping manifests; written confirmation that all intra-group settlements will be made by MT103 wire or ACH/Direct rail, never in physical cash; list of final beneficial owners and all authorized signatories clears PEP screening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FATCA and CRS classification ambiguity for a hybrid tax-exempt foundation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: DGI-issued foreign entity tax residency certificate or null-exemption declaration; CRS self-certification form proving the PIF is a 'Financial Institution' or 'Passive NFFE' as applicable, with granular explanation of any controlling-interest reportable persons; US FATCA Form W-8BEN-E or W-8IMY showing non-US status and such classification; Panamanian legal opinion under Law 25 of 1995 clarifying that the foundation carries a real economic substance activity (warehouse/kitting), not merely passive asset ownership.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound injections into Panama for a PIF must be routed through an SBP-licensed correspondent or domestic clearing bank using SWIFT MT103 wire with a clear beneficiary account designation. A best-practice purpose code should use generic UBO (Unstated Beneficial Owner) or more explicit narrative in field 70, e.g., 'Contribution to Foundation Capital — ISIC 5210 Fulfilment/Kitting' for capital, and 'Trade Payment for Warehousing Services' for operational flows. For capital injections exceeding USD 50,000, the receiving bank will require a board or council resolution authorizing the contribution, a source-of-funds statement certified by the remitter's home bank, and an updated foundation registry certificate. No exchange control approval is required, but corresponding anti-money-laundering declarations must identify the ultimate originating entity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Permissible outbound clearing rails include: (a) SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier settlements and to pay intra-group subcontractors; (b) Commercial Letters of Credit (sight or usance) issued via a Panamanian confirming bank for large kitting raw material imports; (c) ACH/Direct (Panama ACH is USD-denominated via the Panama Automated Clearing House; Nacha-style network only for interbank local credits); (d) documentary collections (cash against documents) for low-risk repeated payments; (e) Airwallex or similar proprietary wallet-to-bank transfers only for non-resident-apocalyptic flows, with parallel reconciliation through a local operational bank. All disbursements must be supported by invoices, inspection reports, or service acceptance certificates to satisfy transfer pricing and AML 'travel-rule' requirements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla USD/foreign-currency outright forward contracts with local commercial banks (for EUR, GBP, CHF, and CNY exposures arising from European and Asian 3PL payables).

Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) on Latin American emerging market currencies (COP, MXN, BRL, CLP) through international banks authorized to deal with non-resident counterparties, not through the local SBP-regulated book.
Cross-currency swaps (USD vs EUR) for the purpose of swapping trade-related receivable flows and matching kitting component imports from Eurozone suppliers.
FX swap agreements with a Panamanian licensed bank for treasury liquidity concentration, provided the counterparty is an authorized dealer and the documentation is registered for tax transparency.

Interest rate swaps are not directly permissible FX instruments unless booked as a combined structure qualifying for the SBP's derivative margin exemptions; standalone FX options are generally permitted for committed trade exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax / Tasa Única (Private Interest Foundation annual government fee)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 March; fixed calendar-year deadline, irrespective of foundation anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment attracts a 10% penalty plus monthly interest (approximately 1% per month); continued non-payment after 30 June triggers administrative suspension and eventual strike-off from the Public Registry after formal notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Registered Agent Appointment Confirmation (Certificación de Agente Residente)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá through the resident registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the anniversary date of the foundation charter (Pacto Fundacional); agent renewal must be continuous
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a registered agent is a violation of Ley 25 de 1995; the foundation may be marked inactive, incur administrative fines, and be liable to strike-off after prolonged non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO and Beneficiary Confirmation (Law 129 of 2020 beneficial-ownership register update)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) through the registered agent's online portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March, plus within 30 calendar days after any change of beneficiaries, foundation council members, or transfer of foundation rights/assets
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: DGI may impose fines up to USD 5,000 for late or inaccurate UBO declarations; repeated non-compliance can lead to administrative suspension and strike-off of the foundation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Not applicable – Panama Private Interest Foundations are not required to undergo a statutory independent audit under Ley 25 de 1995, regardless of asset size, revenue, or number of beneficiaries. A mandatory audit can arise only if the foundation charter expressly requires it or a court orders it in protective proceedings.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS – Panama has adopted IFRS for financial reporting; however, Private Interest Foundations are only required to maintain internal accounting records of assets, liabilities, and operations. No statutory external financial reporting framework is imposed. If financial statements are voluntarily prepared, IFRS is the applicable standard.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Panama's beneficial-ownership regime (Ley 129 de 2020 and implementing regulations), the resident registered agent is the mandatory filer. The foundation must confirm annually the identity of each foundation council member, beneficiary, and protector, if appointed, before the 31 March franchise-tax filing deadline. Any transfer of foundation interests, amendment of the foundation charter, or change in beneficial ownership must be reported to the registered agent within 30 calendar days for immediate DGI registry update.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Foundation Council Members (equivalent of director register)
Register of Beneficiaries and Protector (if appointed)
Minute Book and Resolutions (Libro de Actas)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$450 – US$1,200 per year for resident agent and registered office in Panama
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required; if a voluntary independent review or audit is commissioned, US$1,500 – US$4,000 per engagement

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Private Interest Foundations (PIFs) are not automatically tax-exempt. A PIF engaged in ISIC 5210 kitting, assembly, and fulfillment is subject to Panama's territorial income tax: 25% on net taxable income with Panamanian source. No sector-specific incentive applies to light value-added packaging. However, if the kitting/fulfillment services are physically performed and economically supported outside Panama, the corresponding income is foreign-source and falls outside the territorial tax net, producing a de facto effective rate of 0% on that foreign-source income. Panamanian-source fees are taxed at 25% with no rate reduction.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 700 (Declaración Anual de Rentas) filed through Panama's Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) e-Tax online platform 'Declaraciones en Línea'.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three calendar months after fiscal year-end. For a December 31 fiscal year-end the filing deadline is March 31 of the following year. Advance income tax payments may be required monthly or quarterly during the tax year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax Identification Number (RUC) and full legal name of the Private Interest Foundation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the PIF's Panamanian RUC and exact foundation name; if no RUC has been assigned, complete the provisional registration through DGI and the Public Registry before filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal period start date and end date
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the adopted fiscal year. A PIF may choose calendar year unless already registered with DGI for a different annual period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income from Panamanian source (e.g., kitting and fulfillment fees for services performed in Panama)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all fees for kitting, assembly, and storage services where the physical activities, warehouse, and labor occur in Panama. Such income is taxable even if the client is a non-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source income excluded under Panama's territorial tax system
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only income derived from services performed and assets located outside Panama. Maintain signed contracts, delivery logs, and personnel/payroll evidence to substantiate foreign execution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt income and income already subject to definitive tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use only for statutorily exempt items such as interest on Panamanian government bonds; do not classify kitting fees as exempt solely because the client is abroad.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowed deductions: direct labor, warehouse lease, packaging materials, subcontracting, logistical costs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only deductions incurred in producing Panamanian-source income. Costs allocated to foreign-source activities must be excluded from this line. Keep all invoice and bank payment records.
Compute Panamanian-source gross income minus allowed deductions. A PIF showing no Panamanian-source revenue will normally report zero; do not report negative amounts from foreign activities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable at the 25% statutory headline rate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply 25% to the net taxable income in Box 050. For non-resident PIFs, this applies only to Panamanian-source net income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prepayments, withholdings credited, and advance payments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter Panamanian tax withheld by clients and any monthly advance payments made. Attach the corresponding DGI payment receipts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax due or refund amount
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay any balance through the e-Tax portal. Refund requests are initiated separately through Form 110 and require conclusive source documentation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a surcharge of 10% of the tax due, with additional monthly indexation up to three months and late-payment interest at the statutory rate. Administrative fines range from PAB 50 to PAB 5,000. Persistent non-filing may result in DGI suspension of the RUC, asset freeze orders, and disqualification of the foundation from new business operations.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends declared or distributed out of Panamanian-source profits. Dividends paid from foreign-source accumulated profits are outside Panama's territorial tax and are not subject to the 10% dividend withholding tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Because Panama does not maintain a large double tax treaty (DTT) network, treaty relief is available only under expressly ratified agreements. To invoke DTA relief, the beneficiary must submit to DGI: (i) a written waiver or reduced-rate request, (ii) the certified Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the treaty jurisdiction, (iii) an ownership chain analysis and beneficial ownership declaration, and (iv) the underlying dividend/royalty/interest contract. DGI retains substantive review and may deny relief for shell holding structures lacking economic substance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory: there is no blanket WHT on outbound interest and royalty remittances when the PIF is not deducting a Panamanian-source expense. If the payment is linked to Panama-source business and is deducted locally, Panama may impose a 12.5% gross-base withholding on the payment to the non-resident. Treaty: in the limited DTA network, interest and royalties are typically reduced to 5% or 10%, or exempt if the beneficial owner is not a flagrant conduit and meets treaty limitations.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Balboa (PAB/USD). A PIF engaged in related-party transactions with an aggregate annual value above USD 1,000,000 must prepare and file transfer pricing documentation (Local File). Master File and CbCR must accompany fiscal periods where the multinational group consolidated revenue exceeds USD 50,000,000. Related-party service contracts below the threshold must still follow the arm's length principle and retain contemporaneous six-factor analysis.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's ESR framework (Law 70 of 2019 and related Decrees) applies to entities, including Private Interest Foundations, engaged in geographically mobile activities and claiming tax benefits tied to fiscal domicile. For ISIC 5210 kitting and fulfillment, the PIF must demonstrate real physical presence in Panama or in the treaty jurisdiction: leased warehouse premises, operational staff, inventory management systems, and supervision of core logistics functions. Substance is evaluated proportionately to the value of the fulfillment services. A PIF that merely holds a warehouse address and routes payments through Panama is presumed to be a shell entity and loses access to treaty and territorial-source advantages.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully omitting Panamanian-source kitting fees from Form 700, falsely characterizing warehouse revenue as foreign-source, or maintaining dual books for fulfillment transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty of up to 50% of the evaded tax plus statutory interest and full reassessment. Criminal conviction carries fines of PAB 10,000 to PAB 100,000 and imprisonment from 5 to 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts are authorized to pierce the PIF veil when the foundation is used to evade tax. Directors, officers, and beneficial owners are personally liable for restitution of unpaid taxes, face travel bans and exit restrictions, and may be criminally imprisoned.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the PIF as an empty conduit: no physical warehouse, no employees, no real logistics contracts, and no economic substance in Panama while claiming foreign-source exemption on all fulfillment fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI and the Public Registry may cancel the foundation's registration, freeze its assets, declare the relevant transactions void for tax purposes, and impose fines up to PAB 50,000. The shell classification also triggers automatic exchange of information to the ultimate beneficial owner's tax residence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a shell PIF are jointly and severally liable for taxes, penalties, and interest. Personal asset forfeiture, disqualification from acting as foundations' directors, and five-year entry bans to Panama are enforceable against responsible officers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting related-party kitting or license fees at non-arm's length prices, failing to file the required transfer pricing affidavit, or destroying contemporaneous documentation for intercompany operations above the USD 1,000,000 threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI may recharacterize the related-party transaction, add deemed taxable income under the approved arm's length methodologies, deny expense deductions, and levy a 30% penalty on the transfer pricing adjustment plus interest from the underpayment date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible directors who sign false transfer pricing reports are personally liable for up to 100% of the assessed deficiency when fraud is proven. The same individuals are subject to criminal penalties for fiscal fraud and should expect civil restitution proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting fulfillment and kitting payments on behalf of clients connected to OFAC or EU sanctioned nations, failing to identify the ultimate beneficial owner, or moving proceeds through unlicensed payment rails (e.g., non-monitored Airwallex sub-accounts) without a Panamanian AML/KYC file.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering conviction under Panamanian Criminal Code Article 254 carries imprisonment of 5 to 8 years, asset forfeiture of up to twice the laundered value, and a criminal fine against the PIF of up to PAB 1,000,000. The foundation may also be debarred from international banking counterparties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers of the PIF are personally named in criminal prosecutions if they processed tainted funds knowingly or with willful blindness. Personal assets are subject to freezing, international arrest warrants may be issued, and individuals are barred from future Panamanian fiduciary roles.
